subject.title: Native Codex subagents hit `Native hook relay unavailable` on 2026.6.1 while parent session works

question: When the native Codex PreToolUse relay is unavailable or stale, should OpenClaw refresh/re-register the relay, fall back to generic policy evaluation, or keep unknown relay states fail-closed and improve recovery diagnostics?
rationale: This cannot be safely decided by cleanup automation because the choice changes how native shell, patch, and MCP tool execution is allowed or blocked when the approval relay cannot be reached.

options.title: Refresh Relay, Preserve Fail-Closed
options.body: Prefer relay refresh or re-registration that restores active Codex sessions while keeping unknown or retired relay states fail-closed.

options.title: Accept Generic Policy Fallback
options.body: Allow fallback to generic before-tool policy when the relay is unavailable, but require maintainer security acceptance and live proof that enforcement still fires.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed, Improve Recovery
options.body: Keep the current hard block for unknown unavailable relays and instead add clearer diagnostics, doctor coverage, and documented recovery for affected sessions.

recommendation.title: Refresh Relay, Preserve Fail-Closed
recommendation.body: Prefer relay refresh or re-registration that restores active Codex sessions while keeping unknown or retired relay states fail-closed.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best current routing candidate because they authored or merged the guarded fail-closed fallback and the adjacent generation-preservation repair.
